target.title: fix(channels): stale presence after installing a persisted-auth channel plugin
target.body:
Closes #106646

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who dynamically install a plugin that adds a
channel with persisted auth state (for example a bundled Matrix/Signal-style
channel) would keep seeing the pre-install channel presence list. Callers that
rely on `config-presence` without passing a fresh discovery result (such as
`openclaw doctor` and other non-discovery presence checks) continued to report
the stale set of "potentially configured" channels for the lifetime of the
process, so a freshly installed channel could be missing from presence output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in
`src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never
invalidated, so it could not observe registry changes at runtime. This adds a
small `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` seam and calls it on the successful
plugin install path, so the next presence read re-derives the channel list.
No config shape, protocol, or public presence API changes; the cache remains a
process-local single slot and is only reset when the plugin registry can
actually change.

## User Impact

After dynamically installing a plugin that contributes a persisted-auth
channel, presence detection (including `openclaw doctor`) now reflects the newly
installed channel without requiring a gateway restart.

## Evidence

- New regression test in `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts` reproduces the
  stale-cache behavior: it shows the cached list serving the pre-mutation value,
  then verifies `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` makes the next read return
  the updated channel list.
- Focused suite green locally:

  ```
  $ vitest run src/channels/config-presence.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  7 passed (7)
  ```

- oxlint clean on the three touched files.
- autoreview (Claude) closeout: no accepted/actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `src/channels/config-presence.ts` kept a module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache that was populated on first use and never invalidated. After an operator installed a channel plugin with persisted auth at runtime, presence callers that did not pass a fresh discovery result (e.g. `openclaw doctor`) kept reporting the stale pre-install channel list for the process lifetime. The fix adds `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` and calls it on the successful plugin install path (`src/plugins/install.ts`).

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.9. The invalidation seam is covered by `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`, which asserts the cache is repopulated from the live registry after install.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head. The test suite adds coverage for the invalidation path (`+37` lines in `config-presence.test.ts`), and `install.ts` calls the new seam on success (`+4`).

Observed result after fix: A freshly installed channel with persisted auth now appears in presence output on the next read (the cache is reset on install, then re-derived), instead of being hidden behind a stale cached set.

What was not tested: A full multi-plugin gateway restart was not run; the proof targets the exact changed seam — the cache invalidation call on the install path and its effect on the next presence derivation.
